application_review: PROGRESS. The pair-Gowers-testing round was rechecked before edits. Retained proof source hashes and axiom sets remain unchanged.

The localized generators are actual mixed dual functions, not vectors assumed to possess localized representations. Their nonroot unit inputs have represented Hilbert images in the other closed dual space. The unused root may be set to zero, using an exact nonroot-congruence theorem, so requiring a unit root in the definition does not exclude the original unit-nonroot duals.

The localized subspace is the topological closure of the actual generators span. An orthogonal-projection instance follows from closedness, and no representability or density property is inferred from this instance.

The localized subspace contains the actual constant-one family. Generator containment in the first factor follows from the original cellwise mixed-dual hull, and containment in the positive-degree other factor follows from the actual internal-dual-closure theorem. Closedness of the intersection extends this containment to the whole localized space.

Finite products use the verified exact averaged dual identity. For every selected internal shift array, the new input is a finite product of translated original inputs. Its unit bound and other-factor membership are proved. The selected dual is therefore a genuine localized generator, and the internal-average theorem preserves the original weighted Hilbert law without a bound on parameter cardinalities.

For arbitrary sets of actual unit families, algebraic-span induction constructs an actual preimage in the original family span with one uniform pointwise bound. The bound may depend on the finite span expression and is not asserted uniform across approximations.

The generic multiplier argument checks the algebraic generator span under the composed linear map, then extends through actual dense approximants and the already verified Hilbert distance contraction. Pairwise generator product closure extends first to generator multipliers on the whole space and then, by swapping the factors, to all actual unit represented multipliers in the space.

For the localized generators, the required pairwise product premise is discharged by the actual finite-product theorem. Thus unit-product closure of the new localized space is proved, rather than inserted as a hypothesis.

An actual unit member of the other factor orthogonal to the localized span is paired with its own first-direction pure dual, which is a localized generator. The exact correlation-power identity makes the first Gowers moment tend to zero, and the positive-degree root argument gives vanishing Gowers value and full first-factor orthogonality.

Fourteen theorems, three definitions and one projection instance are audited. This constructs the localized space and proves its algebra and separation properties. The reverse inclusion from the original intersection is not claimed: clipping closure and bounded actual projection representatives for this localized space are still needed. Full higher-order concatenation, qualitative Bessel and the main StrongConjecture remain unproved.
remaining: The common-system master estimates, first-order Bessel, dual energy reduction, recursion and stability are proved. Actual dual functions now have a common finite empirical approximation preserving arbitrary cell probabilities, unit bounds and uniform bounded-test correlations. Exact arbitrary-vertex reflection of the actual subgroup cube law and mixed products is now proved. Mixed cubes now have exact arbitrary-vertex duality and weighted single-vertex replacement estimates. Finite products of dual functions now have quantitative empirical approximation uniform over bounded tests. Exact translated-product expansions and extraction for each fixed test are now proved. The exact mixed face split, projected-face correlation and one-step face Cauchy-Schwarz inequality are now proved. Face energies are now identified with actual copied cube means, with nonnegativity and copy algebra verified. Arbitrary-coordinate permutation invariance, copied-mean nonnegativity and reflection bounds are now established. Full multidimensional mixed Gowers Cauchy-Schwarz, the product-root bound and the single-vertex bound are now proved. Actual dual anti-uniformity, its weighted version and the finite zero-root orthogonality characterization are now proved. Mixed dual recursion, covariance and exact subgroup-shift expansions are now established. Same-subgroup mixed-dual finite products now have an exact averaged dual representation and retain weighted anti-uniformity. The actual unit-input mixed-dual convex hull now has multiplicative and translation closure with unchanged weighted anti-uniform bounds. For varying finite groups and cell types, the exact weighted Haar Hilbert realization and vanishing-Gowers/closed-dual-span orthogonality equivalence are now proved. The dual Hilbert span now has uniformly bounded scaled-hull representatives dense in its closure; their bound may depend on the approximation. Fixed-polynomial and continuous functional calculus for scaled-hull representatives, their clipping closure, and unit-interval-valued approximation of the actual dual Hilbert projection are now proved. The actual dual projection now controls the limiting Gowers power and yields unit-interval models with arbitrarily small Gowers error along the same ultrafilter. For ultrafilters containing every tail, diagonalization now provides one exact unit-interval representative of the dual projection and residual Gowers convergence to zero. Actual unit mixed-dual-hull multiplication now preserves the closed dual space and its orthogonal complement and satisfies the genuine projection pull-out identity on represented inputs. Every unit-bounded actual representative in the closed mixed-dual subspace now multiplies that subspace and its orthogonal complement into themselves. The genuine projection pull-out identity extends to these structured multipliers without requiring cellwise convex-hull membership. Actual translations, with shifts allowed to vary by stage and cell, act linearly on weighted-Haar L2-bounded families, preserve their Hilbert distances, and have inverse-shift adjoints. They preserve the closed mixed-dual subspace and its orthogonal complement; the genuine dual projection commutes with translation on actual represented inputs. Closed Hilbert subspaces containing every selected actual unit family now contain their internal finite averages, using fixed sample counts and the original weighted L2 variance bound. Finite products of unit represented structured inputs remain structured. Taking a mixed dual along any second subgroup system preserves the first closed dual space for such inputs. A unit represented member of the first space orthogonal to the intersection has vanishing second-system Gowers seminorm and is orthogonal to the entire second dual space. For tail-containing ultrafilters and positive degrees, actual dual projections now preserve the other closed dual space and commute on the entire completed Hilbert space. The proof first transfers orthogonality using actual unit-bounded projection representatives, proves unit-interval compatibility and an exact intersection model, then extends closed-space preservation from bounded generators by projection continuity and derives full commutation by self-adjointness. The first-order mixed dual is now identified with actual subgroup Haar averaging. Its unit hull consists of subgroup-invariant functions, and unit invariant functions belong to it. Actual first-order projections have exact unit Haar representatives. The first-order closed dual space is antitone in the subgroup, and its base concatenation is proved as the full equality of the two first-order spaces intersection with the first-order space of the subgroup sum, for every ultrafilter. The actual lower-order recursive coefficient now has a unit-bounded representative in both the lower first-direction dual space and the positive-degree second-direction dual space, for shifts varying by stage and cell. A dependent-selection argument gives uniform small correlation from vanishing correlation for every selected parameter family, without bounded cardinality assumptions. Orthogonality to the lower intersection therefore controls all these recursive coefficients uniformly along the ultrafilter. A tail-containing ultrafilter now supplies a positive uniform testing threshold from null testing of every dependent selected sequence, proved by slow-stage diagonalization. Every selected actual unit family in a positive-degree dual space therefore admits one eventual Gowers threshold controlling all parameters and all unit tests. The result also applies to fixed finite products of structured families and to recursive coefficients under the explicitly displayed lower-space containment. The original cube average is invariant under ambient translation. Averaging a pair-shift multiplicative derivative gives exactly the next cube order, and the corresponding Gowers moment identity preserves the original cell weights. A finite Haar testing estimate bounds mean absolute correlation by epsilon plus the next-order weighted Gowers power divided by a positive threshold power. Under an explicit eventual uniform small-test hypothesis, vanishing next-order Gowers values imply vanishing mean absolute correlation for varying finite subgroup systems along any filter. The actual mixed-dual families with unit inputs represented in the other dual space now generate a defined closed Hilbert subspace. Root normalization is proved harmless. This localized span contains the constant one and is contained in the original factor intersection when the other degree is positive. Finite products of localized actual duals lie in the localized closed span by an exact averaged dual representation and the verified internal-average theorem. Generic unit-generated spans have uniformly bounded actual algebraic-span representatives and dense actual approximants. Unit multipliers whose products with the generators lie in the closed span preserve that span, and pairwise generator closure extends to every actual unit represented member. Consequently actual unit members of the localized span multiply it into itself. An actual unit represented member of the other factor orthogonal to this localized span has vanishing first-factor Gowers value and is orthogonal to the entire first factor. The reverse inclusion identifying the localized span with the intersection remains to be proved; it still requires the clipping and bounded-projection argument for this new space. Higher-order concatenation controlling dual correlations and the full qualitative Bessel theorem remain missing, as do remaining replica integration, cyclic-to-interval transfer and inverse correlator existence. Coloring-derived targets, Calibration/Alignment and final ordered positive rapidly separated monochromatic extraction remain. StrongConjecture is unchanged and unproved. No unavoidable blocker is established; publication, PR and prize application remain pending.
